title: clientapp fails: a shared library was force-removed out from under it, and dpkg's database still doesn't agree with itself
description_md:
`clientapp` fails immediately with `error while loading shared libraries: libfoo.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory`. Digging through shell history, someone ran `dpkg -r --force-depends libfoo1` a while back while "cleaning up unused packages" -- `--force-depends` let dpkg skip the safety check that would normally have refused, since `clientapp` still depends on it. SSH in as `trainee` (passwordless `sudo`), work out what state dpkg's database is actually in now, and restore things properly (not just by copying a file back by hand).

You're done when `clientapp` runs successfully, `apt-get check` reports no broken dependencies, and `libfoo1` is genuinely reinstalled (not just its file quietly replaced).
